31. Five Best Practices for Stable Data Processing稳定数据处理的五条最佳实践

Christian Lauer

克里斯蒂安·劳尔

The following five best practices are the basics when it comes to implementing data processes such as ELT or ETL.

下面五条最佳实践，是实现 ELT 或 ETL 这类数据流程时的基本功。

Prevent Errors防止错误

In case of failure, a rollback should be done—similar to with SQL. If a job aborts with errors, all changes should be rolled back. Otherwise, only X% of the transaction will be transmitted, and a part will be missing. Finding out what that missing data is will be very hard.

失败时应当做回滚——和 SQL 类似。如果一个作业因错误中止，所有变更都应回滚。否则，事务只有 X% 被传输出去，会缺一块数据。要找出缺的是什么数据会非常困难。

Set Fair Processing Times设定合理的处理时长

How long does a job take to process X data rows? This provides important insights about the process. How often and how long does a process have to run? Which data actuality can I assure my department? What happens when data has to be reloaded?

一个作业处理 X 行数据要多久？这会提供关于流程的重要洞见。一个流程要多久跑一次、每次跑多久？我能向部门保证数据的新鲜度是多少？数据需要重载时会发生什么？

Use Data-Quality Measurement Jobs使用数据质量度量作业

Are my source and target systems compliant? How can I be sure that all data has been transferred? Here, I recommend building up a monitoring strategy. It's always a good idea to measure data quality and to detect errors quickly; otherwise, a lack of trust from the consumer can result.

我的源系统和目标系统是否一致？我怎么确定所有数据都传过去了？这里我建议建立一套监控策略。度量数据质量、快速发现错误永远是好事；否则会导致消费方失去信任。

Ensure Transaction Security确保事务安全

When using database-replication software in your process (for example, AWS Data Migration Service, or DMS) instead of a direct connection between system A and system B, you can run into trouble. I once had a replication job that loaded data from table A and table B at the same time. Both were further processed by an ETL job, but if a dataset from table B was not available because of high latency, and the dataset from table A was processed,

当你在流程中使用数据库复制软件（例如 AWS Data Migration Service，即 DMS），而不是系统 A 和系统 B 之间直连时，可能会出问题。我曾经有一个复制作业同时加载表 A 和表 B 的数据。两者都被一个 ETL 作业进一步处理，但如果表 B 的数据集因为高延迟而不可用、而表 A 的数据集已被处理，

— p.81 —

the information from table B would be missing. Here, I also recommend adding monitoring, or dispensing of too many additional components in the process.

表 B 的信息就会缺失。这里我同样建议加上监控，或者去掉流程中过多的额外组件。

Consider Dependency on Other Systems考虑对其他系统的依赖

Various circumstances must be taken into account for the source systems:

对源系统必须考虑各种情况：

  • Availability. When is a source system available? Consider maintenance cycles and downtimes.
    可用性。源系统什么时候可用？考虑维护周期和停机时间。
  • High data load. The target systems must not receive any unnecessary changes (CDC) from the source system; for example, during peak times. Instead, data transfer could take place in a batch job at night.
    高数据负载。目标系统不应在高峰时段接收源系统不必要的变更（CDC）。相反，数据传输可以放在夜间的批处理作业中进行。
  • Unwanted behavior of other systems. As described previously, database replication services could ruin your ETL processes, but other problems also can occur; for example, duplicate and inconsistent data. Here, it is important to get to know the source systems and their pitfalls.
    其他系统的非预期行为。如前所述，数据库复制服务可能毁掉你的 ETL 流程，但其他问题也可能发生；例如重复和不一致的数据。这里关键是要了解源系统及其陷阱。

Conclusion小结

For me, these are the five most important building blocks for establishing a stable and secure data process. You should always keep in mind that data quality is important. Otherwise, you might experience a lack of trust from users and business departments.

对我而言，这是建立稳定、安全数据流程最重要的五个基石。你应当始终牢记数据质量很重要。否则，你可能会面临用户和业务部门的信任缺失。

— p.82 —

32. Focus on Maintainability and Break Up Those ETL Tasks关注可维护性，把 ETL 任务拆小

Chris Moradi

克里斯·莫拉迪

As the data science tent widens, practitioners may excel at using prepared data but lack the skills to do this preparation in a reliable way. These responsibilities can be split across multiple roles and teams, but enormous, productive gains can be achieved by taking a full-stack approach, in which data scientists own the entire process from ideation through deployment.

随着数据科学的帐篷越撑越大，从业者可能擅长使用准备好的数据，却缺乏以可靠方式做这种准备的技能。这些职责可以拆分到多个岗位和团队，但采取全栈方式——让数据科学家拥有从构想到部署的整个流程——可以获得巨大的生产力收益。

Whether you're a data scientist building your own ETLs or a data engineer assisting data scientists in this process, making your data pipelines easier to understand, debug, and extend will reduce the support burden for yourself and your teammates. This will facilitate iteration and innovation in the future.

无论你是在自己搭 ETL 的数据科学家，还是在这一过程中协助数据科学家的数据工程师，让数据管道更容易理解、调试和扩展，都会减轻你和队友的支持负担。这会为未来的迭代和创新提供便利。

The primary way to make ETLs more maintainable is to follow basic software engineering best practices and break the processing into small and easy-to-understand tasks that can be strung together—preferably with a workflow engine. Small ETL tasks are easier for new contributors and maintainers to understand, they're easier to debug, and they allow for greater code reuse.

让 ETL 更可维护的首要方式，是遵循基础的软件工程最佳实践，把处理拆成小而易懂的任务串起来——最好用工作流引擎。小的 ETL 任务对新贡献者和维护者来说更容易理解、更容易调试，也允许更高的代码复用。

Doing too much in a processing step is a common pitfall for both the inexperienced and the highly experienced. With less experience, it can be hard to know how to decompose a large workflow into small, well-defined transformations. If you're relatively new to building ETLs, start by limiting the number of transformations you perform in each task by separating things like joining source tables, creating flag columns, and aggregating the results. You should seek advice and code reviews from those with more experience and the teammates who will help support your ETLs in production. These reviews should focus on simplicity rather than performance.

在一个处理步骤里做太多事，是新手和老手都常犯的错。经验不足时，很难知道如何把大工作流拆成小而定义良好的转换。如果你刚开始做 ETL，可以先限制每个任务里做的转换数量，把“join 源表、创建标志列、聚合结果”这类事情分开。你应该向更有经验的人、以及会在生产中帮你支持 ETL 的队友寻求建议和代码评审。这些评审应聚焦于简单性而非性能。

— p.83 —

Highly experienced data engineers can also produce overly dense pipelines because chains of complex transformations feel commonplace. While this is acceptable if they are the only ones maintaining these ETLs, it prohibits less-experienced data scientists or engineers from supporting, modifying, or extending these pipelines. This can block innovation because the data scientists are reliant on a small number of experts to implement changes.

经验丰富的数据工程师也可能产出过于稠密的管道，因为一连串复杂转换对他们来说习以为常。如果他们是唯一维护这些 ETL 的人，这还可以接受；但这会让经验不足的数据科学家或工程师无法支持、修改或扩展这些管道。这会阻碍创新，因为数据科学家要依赖少数专家来落地变更。

If you're an experienced data engineer, you should consider how easy it is for someone with less experience to understand and build upon your work and think about refactoring so that it's more accessible. Your work doesn't need to be universally understood, but consider how much you and others are gaining from the added complexity.

如果你是有经验的数据工程师，应该考虑经验更少的人有多容易理解和在你的工作之上继续构建，并思考重构以让它更容易上手。你的工作不需要被所有人理解，但要想一想：这份额外的复杂度，到底给你和他人带来了多少收益。

Breaking pipelines into small tasks may carry computational costs as the work can't be optimized across these boundaries. However, we sometimes focus too much on runtime performance when we should instead focus on the speed of innovation that's enabled. In some cases performance is critical, but optimizing a daily batch job to shave an hour off the runtime may add weeks or even months to the time required to implement future enhancements.

把管道拆成小任务可能带来计算上的开销，因为跨这些边界就没法做优化。然而我们有时过于关注运行时性能，而应当关注由此带来的创新速度。某些情况下性能确实关键，但把一个日批作业优化到少跑一小时，可能会让未来增强功能的实现时间增加几周甚至几个月。

— p.84 —

33. Friends Don't Let Friends Do Dual-Writes别让朋友搞双写

Gunnar Morling

冈纳·莫林

Long gone are the times when enterprise application developers could just put data into their application's database and call it a day. Nowadays, data often needs to be persisted in multiple systems in order to satisfy ever-increasing user requirements: changed data needs to be sent to separate search services, enabling a feature-rich full-text search experience usually not provided by databases themselves, and caches need to be updated, allowing for fast data retrieval without accessing the database itself.

企业应用开发者把数据往自己应用的数据库里一写就收工的时代早已过去。如今，为了满足不断增长的用户需求，数据常常要持久化到多个系统：变更的数据要发到独立的搜索服务，以提供数据库本身通常不具备的丰富全文检索体验；缓存也要更新，以便不用访问数据库本身就能快速取数。

But how can all these data stores—an application's database, a search index, a cache—be kept in sync? We might be tempted to simply issue requests to all these systems for updating the data, but here be dragons.

但这些数据存储——应用数据库、搜索索引、缓存——怎么保持同步呢？我们可能会忍不住向所有这些系统发请求去更新数据，但这里有龙。

What if, for instance, the search index temporarily isn't available because of a networking issue? We could think of implementing retry logic, but things quickly get complex there. Worse, even if we are able to successfully update all the involved resources, we might end up with data inconsistencies. Unless all the updates are done within a single global transaction (which, in turn, would tie our service quality to the availability of all the resources), we have no ordering guarantees across multiple data changes. If two updates to the same record occur in close temporal proximity, they could be applied in a different order in the search index than in the database. On the surface, things would look good, but the search index would actually provide incorrect results.

例如，如果搜索索引因为网络问题暂时不可用怎么办？我们可以实现重试逻辑，但事情很快就复杂起来。更糟的是，即使我们成功更新了所有相关资源，仍可能以数据不一致收场。除非所有更新都在单个全局事务中完成（而那又会把我们的服务质量绑在所有资源的可用性上），否则跨多个数据变更就没有顺序保证。如果对同一条记录的两次更新在时间上非常接近，它们在搜索索引中的应用顺序可能与在数据库中不同。表面上看起来一切正常，但搜索索引实际给出的是错误结果。

And that's why friends don't let friends do dual-writes: writes to multiple distributed resources without shared transaction semantics are error prone and will lead to data inconsistencies. But there's hope: if we cannot update multiple resources, we always can update a single one, and that's the application's database. We then can drive the update of the search index, cache, and other secondary systems based on the changes in the database.

这就是为什么朋友不会让朋友搞双写：向多个没有共享事务语义的分布式资源写入，极易出错并导致数据不一致。但还有希望：如果不能更新多个资源，我们总能更新一个——那就是应用数据库。然后我们可以基于数据库中的变更，去驱动搜索索引、缓存和其他二级系统的更新。

— p.85 —

This is where change data capture (CDC) comes in: it allows users to react to all the changes in a database and transmit them as events to downstream consumers. This avoids the issues discussed previously: log-based CDC solutions such as Debezium tap into the database transaction log, extracting all data changes in their exact order of transaction serialization.

这时变更数据捕获（CDC）就登场了：它让用户能响应数据库中的所有变更，并把它们作为事件传给下游消费方。这避免了前面讨论的问题：像 Debezium 这样基于日志的 CDC 方案会接入数据库事务日志，按事务串行化的确切顺序提取所有数据变更。

By propagating change events to consumers through a distributed commit log such as Apache Kafka, the availability concern is also addressed: if a downstream system isn't available for some time, it can simply continue to read change data topics from the point where it left off before. And as the CDC process is asynchronous too, the only synchronously required resource is the database itself.

通过像 Apache Kafka 这样的分布式提交日志把变更事件传播给消费方，可用性问题也得到了解决：如果下游系统有一段时间不可用，它只需从上次离开的位置继续读变更数据 topic。而且由于 CDC 流程也是异步的，唯一需要同步访问的资源就是数据库本身。

Another advantage of propagating change events through a distributed commit log is that other consumers and use cases can be enabled by simply rereading change event topics from the beginning. That way, data can be relayed to any other interested service, and all that without relying on dual-writes.

通过分布式提交日志传播变更事件的另一个好处是：只要从头重读变更事件 topic，就能启用其他消费方和用例。这样数据可以被转发给任何其他感兴趣的服务，而且完全不需要依赖双写。

— p.86 —

34. Fundamental Knowledge基础知识

Pedro Marcelino

佩德罗·马塞利诺

Knowledge is growing exponentially. It is hard to measure the growth of knowledge, especially over a long period of time. However, if we use the number of academic publications as a proxy for knowledge, we can observe that knowledge is doubling every nine years. If you start working today, 20 years from now, when you are in the middle of your career, the amount of knowledge involved in your professional life will be approximately four times more than it is today.

知识正在指数级增长。衡量知识的增长很难，尤其是在很长的时间跨度上。然而，如果用学术出版物数量作为知识的代理指标，我们可以观察到知识每九年翻一番。如果你今天开始工作，20 年后当你处在职业生涯中期时，你职业生活中涉及的知识量将大约是今天的四倍。

This conclusion would be similar (or even more shocking) if we instead consider the number of books published, the number of scientists, or the amount of data created each day as a proxy for knowledge. And that's scary. All knowledge workers, such as data engineers, therefore face a challenge.

如果改用每年出版的书数、科学家人数、或每天产生的数据量作为知识代理指标，结论也差不多（甚至更惊人）。这很吓人。所有知识工作者——比如数据工程师——因此都面临一个挑战。

On the one hand, the growth of knowledge leads to an unmanageable need to keep up-to-date with several new concepts, technologies, and frameworks. On the other hand, knowledge is becoming more transient, and what we learn today may be obsolete tomorrow. Since it is hard to believe that in the near future knowledge growth rates will decrease, all data engineers suffer from this particular curse of knowledge.

一方面，知识的增长带来一种难以掌控的需要：要跟上一堆新概念、新技术、新框架。另一方面，知识变得越来越短暂，今天学的明天可能就过时了。既然很难相信近期知识增长率会下降，所有数据工程师都承受着这种独特的知识诅咒。

Thus, the most important question is, how do we deal with this growth of knowledge?

因此，最重要的问题是：我们如何应对这种知识增长？

One possible answer is to focus on the fundamentals. In a world of constant change, the fundamentals are more important than ever because they provide a fast track to learning new fields of knowledge as they arise. By definition, fundamentals are the primary principles that the rest of the field can be derived from. Thus, if you master the fundamentals, you can master any new emerging field.

一个可能的答案是聚焦于基础。在一个不断变化的世界里，基础比以往任何时候都重要，因为它们为学习新出现的知识领域提供了快车道。按定义，基础是那些可以推导出该领域其余内容的首要原理。因此，掌握了基础，你就能掌握任何新兴领域。

Moreover, the fundamentals have stood the test of time. This is a manifestation of the Lindy effect, which states that the future life expectancy of any nonperishable entity is proportional to its current age. Accordingly, we can conclude that, since fundamentals are an intellectual production (a nonperishable entity) that have lasted a long time, they are likely to continue to last much longer.

此外，基础经受住了时间的考验。这是林迪效应（Lindy effect）的一种体现：任何不会腐坏的事物，其预期未来寿命与它已经存在的时间成正比。据此我们可以得出结论：既然基础是一种智力产物（一种不会腐坏的事物），而且已经存在了很久，它们很可能还会继续存在更久。

— p.87 —

In a world flooded by an immense amount of knowledge, we need to be able to make sense of information, to distinguish what is important from what is unimportant, and, above all, to combine what we know to fuel our learning and keep up the pace. That requires knowledge. Fundamental knowledge.

在一个被海量知识淹没的世界里，我们需要能理解信息、区分重要与不重要，更重要的是：把已知的东西组合起来，驱动学习、跟上节奏。这需要知识。基础知识。

— p.88 —

35. Getting the "Structured" Back into SQL把“结构化”还给 SQL

Elias Nema

伊莱亚斯·内马

Not that many questions in computer science have been circulating for nearly 50 years and are still around. How to write SQL is one of them. Relational databases have dominated the market since the '70s. Then the whole NoSQL movement arose and smoothly evolved into "NewSQL." Recently, all major streaming systems have been adding support for SQL. There must be something really powerful about this language.

计算机科学里能流传近 50 年、至今仍在讨论的问题并不多。怎么写 SQL 就是其中之一。关系数据库从 1970 年代起就主导市场。然后整个 NoSQL 运动兴起，并平滑演化为“NewSQL”。最近，所有主流流式系统都在加 SQL 支持。这门语言一定有某种真正强大的东西。

With great power comes—you know. SQL is so flexible that it allows you to write queries in almost any form and still get results. The problem is that understanding whether the result makes sense usually requires more effort than producing it. You've seen it yourself, "fixing" joins with a DISTINCT statement or counting rows multiple times.

能力越大——你懂的。SQL 灵活到让你几乎能用任何形式写查询，还能得到结果。问题在于：判断结果是否合理，通常比产出结果更费劲。你自己也见过：用 DISTINCT“修复”join，或者对行数重复计数。

I argue that most of this can be avoided by writing queries in a structured manner, optimizing for readability first. So how do you make structure?

我认为，通过结构化地写查询、把可读性放在第一位，大部分问题都可以避免。那么怎么建立结构呢？

First, begin with the end in mind: what should the answer look like? For example, say you want to analyze revenue for a specific sales channel, categorized by regions. See, it's already a prepared SELECT statement. (In this example, I'm using pseudo-SQL to avoid unrelated details.)

首先，以终为始：答案应该长什么样？例如，假设你想分析某个销售渠道的收入，按地区分类。你看，这已经是一句准备好了的 SELECT。（本例中我用伪 SQL，避免无关细节。）

Usually, the main subject would be in the question you are trying to answer. In this example, you want to analyze revenue. So sales is going to be your main entity, the driving table. In FROM, you should always put this table first.

通常，主语就在你试图回答的问题里。在这个例子里，你想分析收入。那么 sales 就是主实体、驱动表。在 FROM 里，你应该总是把这张表放在第一位。

— p.89 —

Now you want to filter for a specific channel. For this, go to the new table, channels. When adding it, think of your query as a tree—the main table is the trunk, and the new table is a branch.

现在你想筛选某个特定渠道。为此，引入新表 channels。加入它时，把查询想象成一棵树——主表是树干，新表是树枝。

The next step is to group results by region. The sales table has only districts. For regions, you need to go to the districts > cities > regions tables. Here your branch would consist of multiple tables.

下一步是按地区分组。sales 表只有 district。要拿 region，你需要走 districts > cities > regions 这一组表。这里你的分支由多张表构成。

The branching metaphor also helps with rules for OUTER joins. Whenever introduced, carry the subject over in all the join conditions until the end of the current branch.

树枝这个比喻还有助于理解 OUTER join 的规则。每引入一个 OUTER join，就要把主语带到所有 join 条件中，直到当前分支结束。

— p.90 —

Of course, we looked at quite a simple query here. And SQL is sophisticated nowadays; you can do a variety of window functions and complex aggregations. However, the structure should come first. So, to make your query structured and pleasant to read by following these steps:

当然，我们这里看的是一个相当简单的查询。如今的 SQL 很复杂，你可以做各种窗口函数和复杂聚合。然而结构应该先行。要让你的查询结构化、易读，遵循以下步骤：

  1. Begin with the end in mind. Think about what your answer should look like.
    以终为始。想清楚你的答案应该长什么样。
  2. Find the main subject. Always put this subject into a FROM statement first. If there is more than one subject, wrap each into a common table expression (CTE) and apply these steps to each of them.
    找到主语。总是把这个主语表放到 FROM 里。如果有多个主语，把每个包进一个 CTE，然后对每个应用这些步骤。
  3. Add tables to the main one, one intent at a time. For example, the intent might be, "All the following JOINs are here to get the region for a sale."
    一次只为一个意图往主表加表。例如意图可能是：“下面这一堆 JOIN 都是为了拿到一笔销售的地区。”
  4. Be careful about your joins. Ensure that the table you add has no more than one row per join condition.
    小心你的 join。确保你加进来的表在每个 join 条件下最多匹配一行。
  5. Move to groupings, analytical functions, and so forth only after you've finished connecting all the data sources.
    在把所有数据源连完之后，再去做分组、分析函数等。

Once you have learned how to get the data you need from different sources and documented it in the form of a readable structure, the query will tell the story of your analysis by itself. More important, that structure will help others to better understand your intentions and trust your results.

一旦你学会如何从不同源拿到所需数据、并用可读的结构记录下来，查询会自己讲出你分析的故事。更重要的是，这种结构会帮助他人更好地理解你的意图、信任你的结果。

— p.91 —

36. Give Data Products a Frontend with Latent Documentation用隐性文档给数据产品做前端

Emily Riederer

艾米丽·里德勒

The rise of DataOps demonstrates the value of bringing DevOps principles to data engineering. Similar, but less explored, is the need to incorporate principles from design and product management into data builds and explicitly craft a good user experience.

DataOps 的兴起展示了把 DevOps 原则引入数据工程的价值。与之类似但较少被探索的，是把设计和产品管理的原则融入数据构建、并刻意打造良好用户体验的需要。

Engineers should think critically about building a "frontend" for their data that makes it easy to understand and intuitive to use. For data, specifically, the frontend is not a traditional UI but rather the lump sum of tools and documents that enable users to understand the intent, lineage, and quality of a dataset.

工程师应当批判性地思考：如何为自己的数据建一个“前端”，让它容易理解、用起来直观。具体到数据，这个前端不是传统 UI，而是一整套工具和文档的总和，让用户能理解一个数据集的意图、血缘和质量。

Of course, building this frontend is no small task, and often data engineers are at full capacity with the technical aspects of their work. However, many of the artifacts that data consumers want can be created with little to no incremental effort if engineers embrace latent documentation: systematically documenting their own thought processes and decision making during the engineering process in a way that can be easily shared with and interpreted by users.

当然，建这个前端不是小事，数据工程师常常在工作的技术方面已经满负荷。然而，如果工程师拥抱“隐性文档”——在工程过程中系统地记录自己的思考过程和决策，并以易于与用户共享、被用户理解的方式呈现——数据消费方想要的许多产物，几乎不需要额外付出就能产出。

The following are examples of latent documentation you can collect for a low-cost data frontend:

下面是一些你可以为低成本数据前端收集的隐性文档示例：

Generate a data dictionary while gathering user requirements在收集用户需求时顺手生成数据字典

When you talk to users about data requirements (you are talking to users, aren't you?), engage them in the process of documenting these requirements (such as variable names and definitions) in a standardized spreadsheet format. This not only saves potential rework by helping you align with your customers at the start, but also can serve as an excellent start to a data dictionary written in the language of the business.

当你和用户聊数据需求时（你是在和用户聊吧？），让他们参与到把这些需求（如变量名和定义）记录成标准化电子表格的过程中。这不仅能通过一开始就与客户对齐来避免潜在返工，还能成为一份用业务语言写成的数据字典的绝佳起点。

— p.92 —

Utilize a hierarchical variable-naming taxonomy使用分层的变量命名分类法

Variable names are the main way users will interact with your data and one of the most critical components of the user experience. Embrace a hierarchical naming structure that reflects your data model. You might consider a structure like ENTITY_ATTRIBUTE_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE; for example, ACCT_ID, ACCT_LOGIN_DT, ACCT_LOGIN_DEVICE_CD for relational data. Taxonomy can both help encode metadata so users interpret field names and intent correctly, and make it easier to program on top of data (e.g., by selecting all fields containing certain common "stubs").

变量名是用户与你数据交互的主要方式，也是用户体验最关键的组成之一。采用一种能反映你数据模型的分层命名结构。可以考虑像 ENTITY_ATTRIBUTE_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE 这样的结构；例如对关系数据用 ACCT_ID、ACCT_LOGIN_DT、ACCT_LOGIN_DEVICE_CD。分类法既能帮助编码元数据，让用户正确理解字段名和意图，也让在数据之上编程更容易（例如选中所有含某些公共“词干”的字段）。

Publicly answer user questions in an FAQ list在 FAQ 中公开回答用户问题

Understanding the InnerSource Checklist by Silona Bonewald (O'Reilly) introduces the concept of passive documentation: answering user questions in public forums such as Slack or GitHub instead of private channels such as direct messages to create a permanent record. This same strategy can be used to develop an FAQ list for data users.

读 Silona Bonewald 的《InnerSource Checklist》（O'Reilly）会引入“被动文档”的概念：在 Slack 或 GitHub 这样的公共论坛回答用户问题，而不是在私信等私有渠道，以留下永久记录。同样的策略可以用来为数据用户建一份 FAQ。

Depending on your workflow, you might also consider the following:

根据你的工作流，还可以考虑以下几点：

Visualize the data pipeline可视化数据管道

Many popular workflow management systems like Apache Airflow and Prefect visualize your data workflow in a directed acyclic graph. While this type of diagram might be intimidating to an average business user, more-advanced data analysts and data scientists could use it to independently trace data lineage should they ever need to more clearly understand metric definitions or access rawer forms of the data.

许多流行的工作流管理系统——如 Apache Airflow 和 Prefect——会把你的数据工作流可视化为有向无环图。这种图对普通业务用户可能有点吓人，但更高级的数据分析师和数据科学家可以用它独立追踪数据血缘，当他们需要更清楚地理解指标定义或访问更原始形式的数据时。

Share your expectations and quality checks分享你的预期和质量检查

Increasingly, engineers are building data-quality checks into their pipelines with tools such as Great Expectations. These tools can not only help validate data and catch errors for downstream users, but also force you to more clearly articulate how you intend the data to behave.

工程师越来越多地用 Great Expectations 这类工具把数据质量检查建进管道。这些工具不仅能帮下游用户校验数据、抓错误，还会迫使你更清楚地表达你期望数据如何表现。

— p.93 —

37. How Data Pipelines Evolve数据管道是如何演进的

Chris Heinzmann

克里斯·海因茨曼

In today's world, there is so much data being generated and so much business value waiting to be discovered. How can a data engineer get that data efficiently into the hands of analysts and data scientists?

今天的世界里产生了海量数据，也有大量业务价值等待被发现。数据工程师如何能高效地把这些数据送到分析师和数据科学家手中？

Enter the data pipeline. Historically, the standard business practice was to set up an ETL pipeline:

数据管道就此登场。历史上，标准业务做法是搭一条 ETL 管道：

  • Extract. Take data from a source system, usually some sort of scheduler to execute code, called jobs.
    抽取（Extract）。从源系统取数，通常用某种调度器执行代码，这些代码叫作业。
  • Transform. Modify the data in some way—for example, ensure consistency in naming, provide accurate timestamps, perform basic data cleansing, or calculate baseline metrics.
    转换（Transform）。以某种方式修改数据——例如确保命名一致、提供准确时间戳、做基础数据清洗，或计算基线指标。
  • Load. Save the data to a target system, usually a data warehouse.
    加载（Load）。把数据保存到目标系统，通常是数据仓库。

The ETL pattern worked well for many years, and continues to work for thousands of companies. If it's not broken, don't fix it. However, traditional ETL can also be intimidating to get started with, and alternatives exist.

ETL 模式多年来运转良好，今天仍在成千上万的公司里发挥作用。如果没坏，就别修它。然而传统 ETL 入门也挺吓人，而替代方案是存在的。

For early-stage businesses still navigating product/market fit, forgo the sophisticated pipeline. Questions will be too varied and answers needed too quickly. All that is required is a set of SQL scripts that run as a cron job against the production data at a low-traffic period, and a spreadsheet.

对于还在摸索产品/市场匹配的早期公司，别搞复杂的管道。问题会五花八门，答案又需要得太快。所需要的只是一组 SQL 脚本，作为 cron 作业在低峰期跑在生产数据上，再加一个电子表格。

For a company in the middle of a growth stage, setting up an extract, load, transform (ELT) pipeline is appropriate. You will have plenty of unknowns and want to remain as agile as possible in both product and analysis. An ELT pipeline is flexible enough to adapt. Grab the source data with a software-as-a-service (SaaS) provider and/or a few simple SQL scripts and put them in

对于处在成长期中段的公司，搭一条抽取-加载-转换（ELT）管道是合适的。你会有大量未知，希望在产品和分析上都尽可能敏捷。ELT 管道足够灵活。用一个 SaaS 提供商和/或几个简单 SQL 脚本把源数据拉下来，作为“原始”数据放进

— p.94 —

the data warehouse sans transforms as "raw" data. The transforms are done on query or built into the different views.

数据仓库，不做转换。转换在查询时进行，或建在不同视图里。

As the business crystalizes, data starts growing exponentially, and measurements mature, the warehouse will need to codify key metrics and data points in a standard fashion to maintain reliability across your growing organization. Set up this pipeline by modifying the ELT flow with a scheduler after the raw data already sits inside a data store. I saw this work well during my time at Grubhub. This leaves you with two data stores, a data lake that serves as a "raw" data store, and a data warehouse containing "transformed" data.

随着业务清晰化、数据指数增长、度量成熟，数据仓库需要以标准方式固化关键指标和数据点，以在不断壮大的组织中保持可靠性。搭建这种管道的方式是：等原始数据已经落在某个数据存储里之后，再用调度器修改 ELT 流程。我在 Grubhub 时见过这种做法运转良好。这样你就有两个数据存储：一个作为“原始”数据存储的数据湖，和一个装着“转换后”数据的数据仓库。

This kind of architecture has the following benefits:

这种架构有以下好处：

  • Data governance becomes easier, as access controls can be different for the raw data and the transformed data.
    数据治理变得更容易，因为对原始数据和转换后数据可以设置不同的访问控制。
  • The transformations allow for active development and precalculation of important business metrics.
    转换层支持积极开发，并预计算重要业务指标。
  • Each piece in the pipeline is much easier to scale.
    管道中的每一部分都更容易扩展。

Complexity and cost are associated with this architecture, so it makes sense only when the business has achieved some degree of scale.

这种架构伴随复杂度和成本，因此只有在业务达到一定规模时才有意义。

Pipelines are constructed to get faster insights into the business from data. This is true no matter the scale. The architecture of the pipeline will depend on the scale of the business as well as how well the company has reached product/market fit. It is valuable to know all kinds of architectures as early decisions affect how easy or hard other architectures will be to implement as the business grows.

管道的存在是为了从数据中更快地获得对业务的洞见。无论规模大小都如此。管道的架构将取决于业务规模，以及公司达到产品/市场匹配的程度。了解各种架构很有价值，因为早期决策会影响业务增长时实现其他架构的难易。

— p.95 —

38. How to Build Your Data Platform like a Product像做产品一样做数据平台

Barr Moses and Atul Gupte

巴尔·摩西、阿图尔·古普特

At its core, a data platform is a central repository for all data, handling the collection, cleansing, transformation, and application of data to generate business insights. For most organizations, building a data platform is no longer a nice-to-have option but a necessity, with many businesses distinguishing themselves from the competition based on their ability to glean actionable insights from their data.

从本质上讲，数据平台是所有数据的中央存储库，负责数据的收集、清洗、转换和应用，以产生业务洞见。对大多数组织而言，建数据平台不再是可有可无的选项，而是必需——许多企业凭借从数据中获取可执行洞见的能力从竞争中脱颖而出。

Much in the same way that many view data itself as a product, data-first companies like Uber, LinkedIn, and Facebook increasingly view data platforms as products too, with dedicated engineering, product, and operational teams. Despite their ubiquity and popularity, however, data platforms are often spun up with little foresight into who is using them, how they're being used, and what engineers and product managers can do to optimize these experiences.

正如很多人把数据本身视为产品一样，Uber、LinkedIn、Facebook 这类数据优先公司也越来越把数据平台视为产品，配有专门的工程、产品和运营团队。然而尽管数据平台无处不在、广受欢迎，它们常常被仓促搭起来，对“谁在用、怎么用、工程师和产品经理能做什么来优化这些体验”缺乏远见。

Whether you're just getting started or are in the process of scaling one, we share three best practices for avoiding these common pitfalls and building the data platform of your dreams.

无论你是刚起步还是正在扩展一个数据平台，我们分享三条最佳实践，帮你避开这些常见陷阱，构建你梦想中的数据平台。

Align Your Product's Goals with the Goals of the Business让你的产品目标与业务目标对齐

When you're building or scaling your data platform, the first question you should ask is, how does data map to your company's goals?

当你在建或扩展数据平台时，第一个该问的问题是：数据如何映射到公司的目标？

To answer this question, you have to put on your data-platform product manager hat. Unlike specific product managers, a data-platform product manager must understand the big picture versus area-specific goals. This is because data feeds into the needs of every other functional team, from marketing and recruiting to business development and sales.

要回答这个问题，你必须戴上数据平台产品经理的帽子。与具体产品经理不同，数据平台产品经理必须理解全局与局部目标。这是因为数据会喂给其他每个职能团队的需求——从市场、招聘到业务发展和销售。

— p.96 —

Gain Feedback and Buy-in from the Right Stakeholders从正确的利益相关者那里获得反馈和支持

It goes without saying that receiving buy-in up front and iterative feedback throughout the product development process are both necessary components of the data-platform journey. What isn't as widely understood is whose voices you should care about.

不言而喻，事先获得认可、并在整个产品开发过程中获得迭代反馈，都是数据平台之旅的必要组成。不太被广泛理解的是：你应该关心谁的声音。

While developing a new data-cataloging system at a leading transportation company, one product manager we spoke with spent three months trying to sell the vice president of engineering on her team's idea, only to be shut down in a single email by the VP's chief of staff.

在一家头部交通公司开发新的数据编目系统时，我们聊过的一位产品经理花了三个月试图向工程副总裁推销她团队的想法，结果被副总裁的幕僚长一封邮件就否决了。

At the end of the day, it's important that this experience nurtures a community of data enthusiasts who build, share, and learn together. Since your platform has the potential to serve the entire company, everyone should feel invested in its success, even if that means making compromises along the way.

归根结底，重要的是这种经历培育出一个数据爱好者社区，大家一起构建、分享、学习。既然你的平台有潜力服务整个公司，每个人都应觉得自己与它的成功利害相关，即使这意味着一路做些妥协。

Prioritize Long-Term Growth and Sustainability over Short-Term Gains把长期增长与可持续性置于短期收益之上

Data platforms are not successful simply because they benefit from being "first-to-market." For instance, Uber's big data platform was built over the course of five years, constantly evolving with the needs of the business, Pinterest has gone through several iterations of its core data analytics product, and LinkedIn has been building and iterating on its data platform since 2008!

数据平台不会仅仅因为“率先上市”就成功。例如，Uber 的大数据平台花了五年时间建成，随业务需求不断演进；Pinterest 的核心数据分析产品经历了多轮迭代；LinkedIn 从 2008 年起就在构建和迭代它的数据平台！

Our suggestion: choose solutions that make sense in the context of your organization, and align your plan with these expectations and deadlines. Sometimes, quick wins as part of a larger product development strategy can help with achieving internal buy-in—as long as it's not shortsighted. Rome wasn't built in a day, and neither was your data platform.

我们的建议：选择在你组织语境下合理的方案，并让你的计划与这些预期和期限对齐。有时，作为更大产品开发战略一部分的速胜，有助于获得内部认可——只要不是短视。罗马不是一天建成的，你的数据平台也不是。

Sign Off on Baseline Metrics for Your Data and How You Measure It为你的数据及其度量方式确认基线指标

It doesn't matter how great your data platform is if you can't trust your data, but data quality means different things to different stakeholders. Consequently, your data platform won't be successful if you and your stakeholders aren't aligned on this definition.

如果你不能信任自己的数据，你的数据平台再好也没用。但数据质量对不同利益相关者意味着不同的东西。因此，如果你和利益相关者在这个定义上不对齐，你的数据平台就不会成功。

To address this, it's important to set baseline expectations for your data reliability—in other words, your organization's ability to deliver high data availability and health throughout the entire data life cycle. Setting clear service-level objectives (SLOs) and service-level indicators (SLIs) for software application reliability is a no-brainer. Data teams should do the same for their data pipelines.

要解决这个问题，重要的是为你的数据可靠性设定基线预期——换句话说，就是你组织在整个数据生命周期内交付高数据可用性和健康度的能力。为软件应用可靠性设定清晰的 SLO 和 SLI 是理所当然的事。数据团队也应该为他们的数据管道做同样的事。

— p.97 —
— p.98 —

39. How to Prevent a Data Mutiny如何防止数据哗变

Sean Knapp (Founder and CEO of Ascend)

肖恩·纳普（Ascend 创始人兼 CEO）

Data teams are on a collision course. We've seen growth in the volume, velocity, and variety of data that leads to more-complex systems, but the most important component of a company's data sophistication is by far the number of people—architects, engineers, analysts, and scientists—able to build new data products, and their efficiency in doing so.

数据团队正处在对撞轨道上。我们看到数据量、速度、种类都在增长，导致系统越来越复杂；但一个公司数据成熟度中最重要的组成部分，是那些能构建新数据产品的人——架构师、工程师、分析师、科学家——的数量以及他们做事的效率。

As enterprises scale their efforts and their teams to build new data products, the interconnectedness and resulting complexity can be paralyzing for these groups. Worse still, they often have conflicting priorities, sending them down a path wrought with conflict. For infrastructure teams, building for scale, security, and cost are of the utmost importance, while engineering teams prioritize flexibility, development speed, and maintainability. Meanwhile, data scientists and analysts are focused on availability and discoverability of data, and connectivity of tools.

当企业扩展构建新数据产品的努力和团队时，相互关联性和由此产生的复杂度可能让这些群体动弹不得。更糟的是，他们常常有相互冲突的优先级，把他们送上一条充满冲突的路。对基础设施团队而言，为规模、安全和成本而建设最为重要；而工程团队优先考虑灵活性、开发速度和可维护性。与此同时，数据科学家和分析师关注数据的可用性和可发现性、以及工具之间的连通性。

Catering to just one group's needs is a guaranteed strategy to incite a "data mutiny," in which internal users create shadow IT organizations with a mandate to move quickly and free themselves from the conflicting priorities. However, new processes and technologies can help bring back this balance of speed and flexibility, without risking scale, security, and maintainability.

只满足一个群体的需求，必然引发一场“数据哗变”：内部用户会建起影子 IT 组织，被授权快速行动，把自己从相互冲突的优先级中解放出来。然而，新流程和新技术可以帮助恢复速度与灵活性的平衡，而不必以规模、安全和可维护性为代价。

With DevOps, we enabled more people than ever before to build increasingly complex software products faster and more safely, by introducing modular architectures, declarative configurations, and automated systems. The same is possible with data, meaning we can apply the lessons we've learned from DevOps to save organizations from falling victim to a data mutiny.

通过 DevOps，我们引入了模块化架构、声明式配置和自动化系统，让比以往更多的人能更快、更安全地构建日益复杂的软件产品。数据领域也可以做到同样的事——我们可以把从 DevOps 学到的教训应用到数据上，把组织从数据哗变中拯救出来。

— p.99 —

Here are some recommendations:

下面是一些建议：

  • Modular architectures. Today's pipelines all too often resemble a bowl of spaghetti, yet it's essential to have well-defined, modularized pipeline designs. Similar to APIs and microservices, having smaller services that focus on distinct stages enables a data-centric approach to pipeline orchestration and allows for greater flexibility.
    模块化架构。今天的管道常常像一碗意大利面，然而拥有定义良好、模块化的管道设计至关重要。与 API 和微服务类似，让更小的服务专注于不同阶段，可以实现以数据为中心的管道编排，并带来更大的灵活性。
  • Declarative configurations. Similar to what we've seen everywhere, from infrastructure to frontend development, building on a platform that deeply understands how data pipelines work allows us to offload a lot more of that complexity to the underlying engine itself. As a result, the use of declarative systems reduces the implementation complexity and maintenance burden.
    声明式配置。与我们在从基础设施到前端开发等各个领域看到的一样，在一个深度理解数据管道如何工作的平台上构建，让我们可以把更多复杂度卸载到底层引擎本身。因此，使用声明式系统降低了实现复杂度和维护负担。
  • Automated systems. Automating many of the manual development steps involved with pipeline creation brings stability, speed, and flexibility to data architectures, regardless of the inevitable changes in data type and applications. Automation lowers the overall design and maintenance costs across the data development life cycle, while improving the quality and reliability of the resulting data pipelines.
    自动化系统。把管道创建中涉及的许多手工开发步骤自动化，会给数据架构带来稳定性、速度和灵活性，无论数据类型和应用如何不可避免地变化。自动化降低了整个数据开发生命周期的总体设计和维护成本，同时提升了产出数据管道的质量和可靠性。

Over the past decade, trends have emerged as engineering teams shifted from monolithic to modular, manual to automated, and imperative to declarative—resulting in more-stable foundations for critical components within businesses. These same trends can be leveraged for data teams, providing harmonious balance among otherwise conflicting goals, and helping to prevent data mutinies. In return, data teams gain the benefits of improved productivity, flexibility, and speed to deliver on new, innovative data products.

过去十年，随着工程团队从单体转向模块化、从手工转向自动化、从命令式转向声明式，出现了这些趋势——为业务中的关键组件提供了更稳定的基础。同样的趋势可以被数据团队利用，在原本冲突的目标之间提供和谐平衡，并帮助防止数据哗变。作为回报，数据团队获得生产力、灵活性和速度的提升，以交付新颖的创新数据产品。

— p.100 —

40. Know the Value per Byte of Your Data了解你数据的每字节价值

Dhruba Borthakur

德鲁巴·博塔库尔

As a data engineer at various data-driven software companies, I observed how new technologies like Hadoop and Amazon S3 enabled product teams to store a lot of data. Compared to earlier systems, these new systems reduced the cost per byte of data so much that it became economically feasible to store terabytes of data without boring a hole in your pocket. It was easy to calculate this metric: divide your total dataset size by its total cost, and you have your cost-per-byte metric.

在多家数据驱动型软件公司做数据工程师时，我观察到 Hadoop、Amazon S3 这类新技术如何让产品团队存储大量数据。与早期系统相比，这些新系统把每字节数据的成本降得如此之低，以至于存储 TB 级数据在经济上变得可行，不至于掏空口袋。这个指标很好算：用数据集总大小除以总成本，就得到每字节成本指标。

Product engineers started to log every event in their applications, without a second thought: "I'll log fine-grained details about each event, even though I really need only one small piece of this information. It's cheap to log, so why bother to reduce the size of my log record?"

产品工程师开始不假思索地记录应用中的每个事件：“我要记录每个事件的细粒度细节，哪怕我实际只需要其中一小条信息。记录很便宜，我干嘛费劲压缩日志记录大小？”

We data engineers were thrilled to flaunt our terabyte sized datasets, comparing our efforts to those of traditional database administrators who typically managed only up to a few hundred gigabytes of data. General Electric's locomotives generate 1TB of data in a single freight route. A Boeing 787 generates half a terabyte per flight. And data engineers help manage this data! This was in the mid-2010s, when enterprises leveraged the rapidly diminishing cost per byte to practically never delete their log data (other than for compliance reasons).

我们数据工程师则兴高采烈地炫耀 TB 级数据集，把自己的工作与传统数据库管理员——通常只管到几百 GB——相提并论。通用电气的机车在一条货运线路上产生 1TB 数据。一架波音 787 每飞一次产生半 TB 数据。而数据工程师帮着管理这些数据！那是 2010 年代中期，企业利用快速下降的每字节成本，几乎从不删除日志数据（合规原因除外）。

Fast-forward to the early 2020s. Today, I am not challenged by the size of the data that I need to maintain. It is the value that the enterprise extracts from the data that is important to me. What insights are we able to extract from our datasets? Can I use the data when I need it, or do I have to wait for it? These considerations are best captured by a new metric, value per byte.

快进到 2020 年代初。今天，需要维护的数据量对我来说不再是挑战。对我重要的是企业从数据中提取的价值。我们能从数据集中提取什么洞见？我需要数据时能立刻拿到吗，还是要等？这些考量最好用一个新指标来捕捉：每字节价值。

For my enterprise, I have my own way to compute value per byte. If a query touches one specific byte of data, the value of that byte is 1. If a specific byte is not touched by any query, the value of that byte is 0. I compute my value per byte as the percentage of unique bytes that were used to serve any query.

在我的企业里，我有自己计算每字节价值的方式。如果一个查询触达某个特定字节，这个字节的价值就是 1。如果某个字节没被任何查询触达，它的价值就是 0。我把每字节价值计算为：被任何查询使用过的唯一字节所占的百分比。

— p.101 —

For my multiterabyte dataset, I found that my value per byte is 2.5%. This means that for every 100 bytes of data that I help manage, I am using only the information stored in 2.5 bytes.

对我的 TB 级数据集，我发现每字节价值是 2.5%。这意味着我帮忙管理的每 100 字节数据中，真正被使用的信息只存在于 2.5 字节里。

What is the value per byte of your enterprise? You might calculate it differently, but if you can increase the value per byte of your system, you can positively impact the data-driven decisions in your enterprise.

你的企业每字节价值是多少？你可能算法不同，但如果你能提高系统的每字节价值，就能对企业的数据驱动决策产生积极影响。

— p.102 —
